obs.craftax_frame: obs[:63, :63] is Craftax's 63x63 agent frame; the last row and column are black padding (the harnesses fix the observation at 64)

human.controls: Arrows move and face. SPACE interacts. TAB sleeps. 1-4 place stone/table/furnace/sapling. 5-7 craft pickaxes, 8-9-0 craft swords (stand next to a table; iron needs a furnace too).

reference.name: PufferLib craftax_classic
reference.parity: full-state trace, every step, scalar no-FMA build, libm bound to V8 ieee754
not_matched: the host reset consumes one NOOP step before the first agent action (PlayTrain draws and steps in the same frame), so a PlayTrain episode is the C episode with a NOOP prepended

Craftax-Classic-Pixels below light_level 0.5, as drawn by the hosts: Craftax adds per-pixel static from state_rng, which game_logic.py sets from the CALLER's step key (rng, _rng = split(rng)) — so its night frame is not a function of the environment state and no environment can derive the key. The RENDERER reproduces it given the key: setNightKey(k0, k1) installs Craftax's state_rng and the static is drawn with a bit-exact threefry-2x32 (74/74 night frames byte-identical, sleeping frames included). No host supplies a key, so what they draw at night is the deterministic dusk image without the static. At light_level >= 0.5 the hosts' frame IS byte-identical to render_craftax_pixels(state).astype(uint8): 147/147 and 120/120 frames, death frame included. See reference/craftax_pixels/README.md
